newsitem.title: UK: LONDON GOLD CLEARINGS RISE SHARPLY IN JULY - LBMA.
newsitem.headline: LONDON GOLD CLEARINGS RISE SHARPLY IN JULY - LBMA.

text.p: Gold's average daily clearing turnover in volume terms rose sharply in July to 37.00 million ounces compared with 32.2 million ounces in June, according to figures from the London Bullion Market Association released on Tuesday.
It was the highest average daily volume figure since 40.3 million averaged in February this year.
The average number of transfers also rose sharply to 1,309 from 1,105 in June making July's average the highest since March this year.
Although the gold price average $324.10 in July against $340.76 in June, the value of transactions averaged $12.00 billion daily against $11.00 billion daily in June.
Despite the lower gold price the average value of transactions was also the highest since March.

The gold fix slumped to its lowest in 12 years at $315.75 per ounce in July 9 following the announcement on July 3 by the Reserve Bank of Australia that it has sold 167 tonnes of gold in the previous six months.
The average volume of silver transactions was just higher at 270.6 million ounces, 0.10 million ounces above the June average.
The number of silver transactions per day rose to 528 from 513 but the daily average value was lower at $1.2 billion compared with $1.3 billion in June.
